words.engDef: being or happening at the end of a process; final
words.example: Our ultimate goal is to establish a secure database system.

words.engDef: fully in agreement; having the consent of all
words.example: The board reached a unanimous decision to approve the budget.

words.engDef: not subject to any conditions; absolute
words.example: Parents show deep and unconditional love for their children.

words.engDef: to remove a cover or mask from, or reveal secrets
words.example: The investigation managed to uncover corruption in the council.

words.engDef: to estimate something to be smaller or less important than it is
words.example: Do not underestimate the complexity of this math puzzle.

words.engDef: to experience or be subjected to something, especially painful
words.example: The patient is scheduled to undergo a major surgery tomorrow.

words.engDef: a university student who has not yet received a first degree
words.example: She is a second-year undergraduate studying marine ecology.

words.engDef: to draw a line under a word, or emphasize something
words.example: The teacher used a red marker to underline the key words.

words.engDef: lying or situated under, or forming the basis of something
words.example: We must identify the underlying cause of the system failure.

words.engDef: to damage or weaken someone or something gradually
words.example: The constant criticism threatened to undermine his confidence.

words.engDef: situated directly below or under something
words.example: She found a shiny silver dime underneath the rug.

words.engDef: a road or pedestrian passage running underneath a highway
words.example: The pedestrians used the secure underpass to cross the street.

words.engDef: to commit oneself to and begin a enterprise or responsibility
words.example: The research team decided to undertake a thorough survey.

words.engDef: currently in progress or motion
words.example: The scientific expedition to the island is already underway.

words.engDef: clothing worn under other clothes, typically next to the skin
words.example: He packed some clean cotton underwear for the weekend trip.

words.engDef: to cancel or reverse the effects of a previous action, or untie
words.example: Press this button on the remote to undo the last action.

words.engDef: without any doubt; certainly
words.example: She is undoubtedly the most gifted student in our class.

words.engDef: the state of being unemployed, or number of jobless people
words.example: The economic recession led to a sudden rise in unemployment.

words.engDef: to open or spread out from a folded state, or reveal over time
words.example: We watched in suspense as the dramatic plot began to unfold.

words.engDef: the process of being united or made into a whole
words.example: The treaty paved the way for the peaceful unification of the states.

words.engDef: to make or become united, uniform, or whole
words.example: The leader made a grand speech to unify the citizens.

words.engDef: the action of joining together, or an organized association of workers
words.example: The trade union negotiated with management for higher wages.

words.engDef: being the only one of its kind; unlike anything else
words.example: The historic tower is a unique landmark of the city.

words.engDef: to come or bring together for a common purpose or action
words.example: The two political parties decided to unite to defeat the rival.

words.engDef: the state of being united or joined as a whole
words.example: The president called for national unity in his speech.

words.engDef: applicable to all cases; general or global
words.example: Freedom of speech is a universal human right.

words.engDef: to undo the lock of something using a key
words.example: He used a brass key to unlock the wooden door.

words.engDef: never done or known before; completely unique
words.example: The tech startup achieved unprecedented success this year.

words.engDef: to remove a veil or cover from, or reveal a plan publicly
words.example: The company plans to unveil its new smartphone next week.

words.engDef: to make something more modern or up to date with new facts
words.example: The technician updated the database to ensure security.

words.engDef: to raise something to a higher standard or status
words.example: We decided to upgrade our computer network for faster speed.

words.engDef: strictly vertical or honorable in character
words.example: He is an upright gentleman who is held in high esteem.

words.engDef: an act of active resistance or rebellion
words.example: The military dictatorship crushed the popular uprising with force.

words.engDef: moving, pointing, or leading to a higher place or level
words.example: There has been an upward trend in technology stock prices.

words.engDef: towards a higher place, level, or position
words.example: The path sloped upward toward the mountain cliffs.

words.engDef: relating to, or characteristic of a town or city
words.example: The city is planning new public transit for the urban area.

words.engDef: to try earnestly or persistently to persuade someone to do something
words.example: She felt a sudden urge to travel around the world.

words.engDef: the state of being urgent; an immediate need
words.example: The doctor spoke with a sense of urgency about the operation.

words.engDef: requiring immediate action or attention
words.example: The patient is in urgent need of a kidney transplant.

words.engDef: the action of using something, or the way in which a word is used
words.example: The manual provides a clear guide on grammar and word usage.

words.engDef: to guide or escort someone in a direction
words.example: The usher guided the wedding guests to their seats.

words.engDef: a tool or container, especially for household or kitchen use
words.example: Keep the wooden spoon and other kitchen utensils in the drawer.

words.engDef: the state of being useful, profitable, or beneficial; public service
words.example: The monthly utility bill includes electricity and water charges.

words.engDef: to make practical and effective use of something
words.example: The farm utilizes wind turbines to generate clean electricity.

words.engDef: complete or absolute, or to express aloud
words.example: She lay in bed, unable to utter a single word in surprise.
